source.needle: pub fn select_pair(tickets: &[Ticket], now: i64) -> Option<(&Ticket, &Ticket)> {

flow: The pure selector filters live waiting tickets, sorts deterministic anchors and checks both rating windows within one pool.
The durable tick transaction rechecks locked tickets and ratings after lock waits, creates a rated game and changes both tickets to permanent Playing bindings together.
The game-server matcher invokes tick on a one-second interval, alternates the first pool and performs a bounded batch without requiring another join.

guarantees.statement: Pairing skips an incompatible head, uses the oldest compatible anchor and nearest opponent with age/UUID/owner tie breaks, requires distinct users and one pool, and applies both widening windows.
The server chooses the game and permanent Black/White bindings. Pair formation and two ticket transitions commit together; concurrent matchers have one durable winner.
Expired tickets cannot pair, including when expiry occurs during rating-lock waits.

The actual game-server runs matching periodically so a waiting pair can become eligible without another join; each batch alternates starting pool, caps attempts at 32 and stops after two empty pools or a failure.

contracts.statement: Unrated rating is effectively 1500; allowed difference starts at 100 and increases by 50 per complete 30 seconds to 400, using wide arithmetic.

source.needle: async fn tick(&self, pool: Pool) -> Result<Option<GameId>, MError> {

evidence.reason: Concurrent ticks produce exactly one game, one rated_game and two slots, and one user's current participation is Playing. This test does not compare participant or side bindings.
Injected slot failure leaves zero game/rated/slot rows and both waiting; successful retry freezes original Unrated states.
Tickets expire while blocked on rating locks; tick returns None and creates no game.
After aging enqueue times, one/two pair while an incompatible head remains waiting.

contracts.gap: The selected tests do not compare both ticket side bindings with the committed game's participant bindings. The executable test checks snapshot users, but does not compare ticket-side equality.

contracts.statement: The executable uses a one-second skipped-tick interval, alternates starting pools, tries at most 32 ticks and stops a batch on two empty pools or first failure.

evidence.reason: Launches the actual game-server binary and observes waiting tickets become Playing with a sequence-zero snapshot containing both users, without another join.

contracts.gap: The test ages DB timestamps instead of waiting 30 real seconds. It does not assert two-pool fairness, the 32-attempt cap, error logging/recovery or Ctrl-C shutdown.

limitations: The process test proves periodic progress for its one-pool case; pure tests directly assert tie-break policy and do not prove production fairness or timing under load.
Pool names do not enable clocks or time-control adjudication.
Links and passing tests do not establish semantic completeness; changes to guarantees, evidence strength and decomposition require review.
